---
title: "08. Study Area analysis CRS"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{08. Study Area analysis CRS}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Analysis setup records the analyst's projected horizontal coordinate system before
terrain mosaicking. Map display stays in its display CRS. Source geometry and
elevation values are not rewritten when a choice is saved.

In 9033 the default is a searchable EPSG picker. On each opened context,
`study_analysis_crs_server()` calls `fluvgeo::study_crs_candidates()` using the
saved boundary. The backend reads sf's installed PROJ SQLite database through
GDAL; no RSQLite dependency or remote catalog request is needed. It checks layout
compatibility and joins projected definitions to datum, axis units, scope and area
of use. Full geographic-bound coverage is distinguished from partial overlap;
the latter is opt-in. Dateline/global extents wider than 180 degrees route to
explicit review rather than an inferred zone.

The default list contains engineering/topographic scopes and UTM systems, ordered
by coverage and area specificity, with no automatic choice. Other mapping purposes
are opt-in. EPSG:3857 is excluded from recommendations. Unit filtering and name/code
search do not change source data. Selection displays reference details and a link
to SpatialReference.org; a separate Explorer link encodes the Study Area bounds
only when the analyst follows it. An NGS modernization link is always available.

Candidate metadata is discovery evidence, not transformation certification. The
UI shows PROJ/GDAL and EPSG catalog versions, plus the number of locally listed
2022-frame candidates in the region. Dynamic/2022 frames remain explorable but
validation blocks saving pending a qualified coordinate-epoch workflow. Advanced
definitions use the same backend guard. No datum, grid or software substitution
occurs. The advanced text input is optional rather than the normal selection path.

The server verifies candidate membership in the currently filtered list, and binds
checked definitions to mode and context revision. Filtering a checked candidate
out or changing the input/mode invalidates saving. Saved picker evidence adds the
EPSG identifier, catalog version/date, PROJ version, coverage and reference URL to
the automatically generated record. Current persistence is WKT plus action evidence; it
does not introduce a horizontal coordinate-epoch registry. The separate vertical
target table described in article 09 does record intended epoch/model metadata.

`mod_study_server()` supplies current study state, pending-edit checks and an
`on_saved` callback to `study_analysis_crs_server()`. Check CRS calls
`fluvgeo::validate_study_analysis_crs()` and binds its result to the exact input
and context revision. The backend resolves a projected 2D definition and checks
the saved boundary can transform without ballpark operations. It cannot establish
that a projection's distortion is acceptable; that remains an analyst decision.

In 9034 selection/units and filters share horizontal rows; details and background
use disclosures. Check/save buttons are adjacent. The form has no Recorded by or
Why fields. The app generates validation/catalog evidence and records a user
action without claiming an authenticated identity or analyst approval.

Saved acquisition selections remain authoritative while hidden renderUI inputs
are NULL (not initialized). An explicit empty selection remains a pending edit.
This prevents reopening a Study Area from falsely blocking its CRS save.

Save requires current validation, then calls
`store$set_analysis_crs()` -> local `revise()` with injected writer
`fluvgeo::set_study_analysis_crs()`. The writer uses the existing horizontal
analysis_reference row for canonical WKT. Other components, geometry and source
files remain intact. The callback rereads a newly saved context, updates current
state and refreshes the catalog. Pending edits and stale revisions cannot save.

Success appears beside Save only after that persisted reread. Reopening displays
the saved EPSG identifier, or canonical WKT when no identifier exists, in the
authoritative-definition mode rather than leaving an empty picker. The picker
remains available for choosing a replacement. Article 01 describes per-tab reload
restoration; neither checking nor merely changing the form writes a revision.

The store's read path revalidates canonical WKT against the current boundary;
unresolved legacy prose does not count as a configured CRS. Product migration is
not implemented: existing terrain_processing records block CRS changes.

The DEM attempt lookup permits metadata-only study revisions after checking the
current Stream geometry and Collection evidence against the retained selection.
The attempt still binds to its original selection/context, so a CRS save does not
hide unchanged original downloads or rewrite their provenance.

This increment does not expose Event settings or execute masks/mosaics. Vertical
reference/epoch specification now precedes those controls; see the maintained
vertical-reference design. The subsequent Event
contract requires one user-selected output cell size per Event and one Study Area
grid anchor. All same-size Event grids share cell boundaries; source resolution
is recorded separately and does not dictate the chosen output resolution.

Source: `R/study_analysis_crs.R`, `R/mod_study.R`, `R/study_store.R`, and sibling
fluvgeo `R/study_analysis_crs.R`. Focused tests: `test-study-analysis-crs.R`,
`test-stream-dem-files.R`, and backend `test_study_analysis_crs.R`.
